text:
alex nguyen: Heads-up — ran into a case where a high-tier EU request fell back to a smaller quantized variant. We need the console to show the exact routing decision path (policy match, capacity, cost heuristic) so support can explain to customers quickly.

maya singh: +1. Right now the trace just shows final model id. Need ‘decision timeline’ that shows: input headers, policy checks (tier/region), capacity lookup, and fallback reason.

samir patel: Agreed. For a quick win we could surface a small expandable panel on request traces that lists the routing headers and the checks that passed/failed. Something like:

```
X-Redwood-Routing: tier=premium;region=eu-west-1;preferred_model=redwood-13b
Routing-decisions: policy=premium-eu,true;capacity=insufficient,false;cost-boundary=ok,true
Selected-model: redwood-7b-q4f16-fallback
```

That plus a link to the capacity snapshot should be enough for initial support triage.

jenny cho: Love the header idea. UX note: mark the failing check in red with a tooltip explaining "insufficient capacity" vs "higher latency" vs "explicit override". Also include quick actions: reroute to another region, reopen in canary, or force primary model for debugging.

tom h: Implementation constraints: routing decisions are computed in the gateway (edge) then a centralized router may change based on latest capacity. We need consistent request IDs to correlate the edge decision with the router fallback. Add `x-rw-decision-id` in headers.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: added header x-rw-decision-id to gateway output in canary (edge/gw-v2). YAML diff: `+ headers: - x-rw-decision-id`

alex nguyen: Good. Does anyone have a mockup of how the console panel should look? I sketched something: one-line summary (Selected model + reason), timeline of checks, capacity link, and raw headers expandable.

maya singh: I'll drop a quick Figma snippet later, but for telemetry the backend needs to store a tiny decision blob per request (2-4 keys) rather than full routing config to avoid storage blowup. Fields: decision_id, policy_id, checks=[{name,status,reason}], selected_model, fallback_used.

samir patel: +1 on compact blob. Also add a risk_score field when fallback happens (0-100) so console can highlight high-risk regressions in rollouts. That ties into Optimize alerts.

observability-bot: trace created: https://console.redwood/internal/trace/1831004829?decision_id=rw-ff3b9c (shows routing-decision panel available in canary)

jenny cho: UX question: should the decision panel be on by default for all requests or only show when a fallback occurred? My vote: default collapsed, auto-expand when fallback or policy mismatch.

tom h: One more dev detail — we must redact customer PII from headers before persisting. Only keep tier, region, model ids, and boolean checks. Add a sanitization step in gateway.

alex nguyen: OK plan: 1) Gateway emits x-rw-decision-id and compact decision blob to traces (canary edge). 2) Backend stores sanitized blob and links to trace. 3) Console adds a collapsed "Routing decisions" panel that auto-expands on fallback and shows checks + quick actions. 4) Add a support view that surfaces recent fallback counts per customer and risk_score.

samir patel: I'll own the backend blob schema and storage TTL. Target TTL 7 days by default, 30 days for enterprise customers.

maya singh: I'll prototype the panel and the tooltip content. 2-day spike.

alex nguyen: Thanks — tagging for follow-ups: @maya singh for UI, @samir patel for backend schema, @tom h for gateway changes. We'll sync in eng-platform tomorrow 10:30.

jenny cho: :thumbsup:
